about: The phone screen's robot (src/phone/PhoneScene.tsx): the Throughput Subcommittee from Decide, with real hands so it can take the phone by its sides. Made again on 2 Nov with its turnstile moved from its waist to its shoulders and a speed gate's cabinet for a body: David found the waist turnstile read badly ("it looks a little inappropriate"), asked for a reconcept in Tripo, and chose "4th (turnstile as its shoulders)... if you add the speed gate to it", then "Ship it".
credits: 65: image to 3D at 45 and a humanoid rig at 20. The concept edits and the preset animations were free. (The first version, 30 Oct, cost another 65: 7,905 -> 7,840.)

subcommittee.concept: Tripo Studio's image editor, Nano Banana 2 (Gemini), on the hands concept (research/station-assets/phone/subcommittee-hands.jpg), in steps; each prompt follows. Two later edits asked for the glass flaps higher on the shell and changed nothing David kept ("just leave the flaps the last place I saw them"). The concept itself stays in Tripo: https://studio.tripo3d.ai/workspace/generate/99f2d5cd-f77d-4a23-8875-c2f3a2367f1c
prompt: Remove the turnstile hub and the three metal turnstile arms from the robot's waist completely, so nothing sticks out from its waist, hips or the front of its body; its waist is now a plain smooth navy post. Instead, the turnstile is at the top of its body: a round brushed-metal turnstile hub sits at its upper chest just below the counter screen, and its three turnstile bars are its shoulders and collar, two reaching out sideways as the tops of its shoulders and one pointing straight backward behind its neck, none pointing forward. Keep everything else exactly the same: the boxy navy head with its two small square glowing cyan eyes and antenna, the glowing blue counter screen on its chest, its arms and big mechanical hands with glowing blue fingertips, its two short legs and big flat feet, its pose, colors, materials, lighting, framing and plain light grey background. No text, no letters, no numbers.

Keep the turnstile across its upper chest and shoulders exactly as it is, the round hub and its three bars. Change only its body below the chest: replace the thin turnstile post with the sleek pedestal of a modern station speed gate, the kind of ticket gate with glass flaps: a smooth rounded navy cabinet for its torso and waist, with a thin glowing blue light strip running down each side, and two small tinted glass flap panels folded flat against its sides at hip height, lying along its body and pointing backward, never forward. Nothing sticks out from its waist, hips or the front of its body. Keep everything else exactly the same: the boxy navy head with its two small square glowing cyan eyes and antenna, its arms and big mechanical hands with glowing blue fingertips, its two short legs and big flat feet, its pose, colors, materials, lighting, framing and plain light grey background. No text, no letters, no numbers.

Make the speed-gate pedestal body shorter so it ends at hip height, and give the robot back its two short, jointed robot legs below it, with visible knee joints and big flat feet, the legs clearly separate from each other with a gap between them, as they were before, so it can walk. Keep the glowing blue light strips and the two glass flaps flat against its sides, and keep the turnstile across its upper chest and shoulders, the head, arms and hands exactly as they are. Nothing sticks out from its waist, hips or the front of its body. Same pose, colors, materials, lighting, framing and plain light grey background. No text, no letters, no numbers.
